cards.back: Rank, Pack, Prompt, Generate, Check, Ship, Log.
A cross-encoder reranks the top 20 and keeps the best 5. If the best score is under a threshold, don't answer: say not found, ask to clarify or widen the search.
In code, not the prompt, so the model cannot guess from weak evidence.
Remove duplicates, fit a token budget (about 4K), put the strongest chunk first, keep id, source and date with each chunk.

cards.front: Why wrap chunks as data in the prompt
cards.back: Tags like <doc id="c12"> let the model cite ids and are the defence against indirect prompt injection.
Structured output such as {answer, citations: [ids], found}, streamed so first words arrive in about a second.
Every cited id was retrieved and is visible to the user, every number appears in a chunk or tool result, and a safety scan passes. On failure, regenerate once, then fall back.
One trace per request: query, chunk ids and versions, scores, prompt version, model, latency, cost and feedback.
Bi-encoder: separate vectors, precomputed, millions → 20. Cross-encoder: reads both together, accurate but slow, 20 → 5.
Embeddings rank a "30-day free trial" chunk highly; a cross-encoder sees it doesn't answer a refund question, scores it about 0.1 and lifts the refund policy to about 0.9.

quiz.q: The best reranked chunk scores below the threshold. What should the system do?
choices: Answer anyway from the top chunk
Say it could not find the answer, or ask a clarifying question
Lower the threshold for this query
Send all 20 chunks to the model
quiz.why: The gate stops the model guessing from weak evidence.

quiz.q: Why put the strongest chunk first when packing?
choices: Models attend less to the middle of long contexts
It reduces embedding cost
Citations only work for the first chunk
Rerankers require it
quiz.why: Position matters, so the best evidence goes first.

quiz.q: What defends against indirect prompt injection in retrieved text?
choices: Putting chunks before the instructions
Removing chunk ids
Raising the temperature
Wrapping chunks as tagged data after the instructions
quiz.why: Retrieved text is treated as evidence, not instructions.

quiz.q: Which of these is a code check after generation?
choices: Ask the model whether it is confident
Re-embed the answer
Every cited id is a chunk that was retrieved
Check the answer length
quiz.why: Code verifies citations and numbers before anyone sees them.

quiz.q: Why not use a cross-encoder for first-stage retrieval?
choices: It is less accurate than a bi-encoder
It runs once per (question, chunk) pair and cannot be precomputed
It cannot output a score
It only works with keyword search
quiz.why: That is why it only reranks the top 20.

quiz.q: A check fails after generation. What is the fallback order?
choices: Regenerate once, then fall back
Regenerate until it passes
Ship with a warning
Ask the user to verify
quiz.why: One retry, then a safe fallback.
